## 1. Background information on the procedure

## 1.1. Type II variation

Pursuant to Article 16 of Commission Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008, Astellas Pharma Europe B.V. submitted to the European Medicines Agency on 09 March 2026 an application for a variation.

The following changes were proposed:

| Variation(s) requested   | Variation(s) requested                                                             | Type              |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| C.6.a                    | C.6.a) Addition of a new therapeutic indication or modification of an approved one | Variation type II |

Extension of indication to include Padcev, in combination with pembrolizumab, as neoadjuvant treatment and then continued after radical cystectomy as adjuvant treatment, is indicated for the treatment of adults with muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are eligible for cisplatincontaining chemotherapy, based on the results from Interim Analysis 1 of the pivotal Study KN-B15 (EV-304); this is a phase 3, randomized, open-label study to evaluate perioperative enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (MK-3475) versus neoadjuvant gemcitabine and cisplatin in cisplatineligible participants with Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer. As consequence, sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.8, and 5.1 of the SmPC have been updated; the Package Leaflet is updated accordingly. Version 6.1 of the RMP is submitted, to reflect the updated data.

The requested variation(s) proposed amendments to the Summary of Product Characteristics and Package Leaflet and to the Risk Management Plan (RMP).

## Information relating to orphan designation

The new indication, which is the subject of this application, does not fall within any orphan designation.

## Information on paediatric requirements

Pursuant to Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006, the application included an EMA Decision EMEA-002299- PIP01-17; Decision Number: P/0114/2018) product-specific waiver/class waiver covering the extension of indication for the treatment of urothelial carcinoma.

## Information relating to orphan market exclusivity

## Similarity

Pursuant to Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No. 141/2000 and Article 3 of Commission Regulation (EC) No 847/2000, the MAH did not submit a critical report addressing the possible similarity with authorised orphan medicinal products because there is no authorised orphan medicinal product for a condition related to the proposed indication.

## Scientific advice

The MAH did not seek Scientific Advice at the CHMP.

## 2. Scientific discussion

## 2.1. Introduction

## 2.1.1. Problem statement

## Disease or condition

The applied indication is:

Padcev, in combination with pembrolizumab, as neoadjuvant treatment and then continued after radical cystectomy as adjuvant treatment, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are eligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy.

## Epidemiology

Bladder cancer is the ninth most common cancer globally. Incidence varies across regions, with highest crude rates in Europe and North America 1 . The disease is most common in male. The most important risk factor for bladder cancer is tobacco smoking, followed by occupational exposure to aromatic amines and ionising radiation 2 . Lynch syndrome may also predispose to urothelial cancer.

2 Burger M, Catto JW, Dalbagni G, et al. Epidemiology and risk factors of urothelial bladder cancer. Eur Urol. 2013;63(2):234-241.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Biologic features

More than 90% of urothelial tumors have origins in the bladder, the rest from the renal pelvis (8%) and from ureter and urethra (2%). Urothelial (transitional cell) carcinoma is the most common histologic subtype of bladder cancer. The majority of muscle invasive tumors are high-grade urothelial carcinomas 3 .

## Clinical presentation

Approximately 70% of patients with bladder cancer are initially diagnosed with non-muscular invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), which can generally be treated with local procedures and carries overall good prognosis. Approximately 25% are diagnosed with muscular invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) at presentation and another 10% will progress from non-muscle-invasive tumors. Approximately 5% of patients have metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis 4 .

Resectable MIBC is a heterogeneous disease, which ranges from cT2 (invasion of the muscularis propria) to cT4a tumors (invasion beyond the bladder/into adjacent organs) and N0 (no lymph node metastasis) to N1 (unilateral pelvic lymph node metastasis). Higher T stage and lymph node positivity are independent indicators of poor prognosis 5 . The current staging system is AJCC TNM 8 th edition, 2017.

Staging after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) and radical cystectomy (RC) can be done (ypTNM); ypT0N0 after NAC and cystectomy is associated with better prognosis 6 .

## Management

Radical cystectomy (RC) with pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND) with its associated urinary diversion is the standard treatment of resectable MIBC with curative intent 7 . According to ESMO guidelines, 3 to 4 cycles of cisplatin-based neoadjuvant ChT should be given for MIBC, being cisplatin-gemcitabine (CG) or accelerated methotrexate, vinblastine, adriamycin and cisplatin (MVAC) the most widely used neoadjuvant chemotherapy regimens. For those who have received neoadjuvant chemotherapy, there is no role for adjuvant treatment (chemotherapy or RT). Neoadjuvant chemotherapy is preferred, as there is weak evidence to support the use of adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy in patients who did not receive neoadjuvant therapy 8 . Adjuvant nivolumab for 1 year versus placebo after radical resection showed DFS improvement vs placebo in CHECKMATE-274 9 , leading to EU approval in April 2022 in muscle invasive urothelial carcinoma with tumour cell PD-L1 ≥1%, who are at high risk of recurrence after undergoing radical resection 10 . The NIAGARA phase III study showed a statistically significant improvement in EFS and OS with perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant cisplatin + gemcitabine compared with neoadjuvant cisplatin + gemcitabine followed by RC + PLND (EFS: HR 0.68; 95% CI: 0.56, 0.82;

Approximately 50% of all newly diagnosed patients with MIBC are considered eligible to receive cisplatin-based chemotherapy 13 . Cisplatin ineligibility is defined as meeting at least one of the following globally accepted criteria: GFR ≤ 60 mL/min; ECOG ≥ 2; CTCAE v4 Grade ≥2 for audiometric hearing loss or peripheral neuropathy; or NYHA Class III heart failure 14 .

Despite the latest improvements in EFS and OS, recurrence rates and mortality of patients with cisplatin-eligible MIBC are high, and therefore effective therapies with improved long-term outcomes are relevant.

## 2.1.2. About the product

## Pharmacotherapeutic action

Enfortumab vedotin, also referred to as ASG-22CE and Padcev, is a Nectin-4 directed ADC comprised of a fully humanized anti-Nectin-4 IgG1 kappa mAb conjugated to the small molecule microtubule disrupting agent, MMAE, via a protease-cleavable maleimidocaproyl vc-linker. Conjugation takes place on cysteine residues that comprise the interchain disulfide bonds of the antibody to yield a product with a drug to antibody ratio of approximately 3.8.

Enfortumab vedotin binds to the V domain of Nectin-4 protein. Nectin-4 is expressed in multiple cancers, particularly those of epithelial origin such as urothelial cancers.

Enfortumab vedotin induces cytotoxicity in cancer cells by binding Nectin-4 target on the cell surface and forming an ADC-Nectin-4 complex. This complex internalizes and traffics to lysosomal vesicles where MMAE is released by proteolytic cleavage of the vc-linker. Intracellularly released MMAE subsequently disrupts tubulin polymerization and leads to mitotic arrest and apoptosis of tumor cells through direct and bystander-mediated cytotoxicity. Through these mechanisms, enfortumab vedotin has been shown to induce immunogenic cell death in Nectin-4 positive tumor cells.

## Previously approved indications

Padcev is approved for the following indications:

Padcev, in combination with pembrolizumab, as neoadjuvant treatment and then continued after radical cystectomy as adjuvant treatment, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with resectable muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are ineligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy

Padcev, in combination with pembrolizumab, is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic urothelial cancer who are eligible for platinum-containing chemotherapy.

## 2.2. Non-clinical aspects

No new non-clinical data have been submitted in this application, which was considered acceptable by the CHMP.

## 2.2.1. Ecotoxicity/environmental risk assessment

No updated environmental risk assessment (ERA) was performed within the present extension of the indication application.

## 2.2.2. Discussion on non-clinical aspects

Previously evaluated ERA data considered all patients with bladder cancer as eligible for treatment with enfortumab vedotin. As the present application does not alter any of the parameter used for the ERA of the previous extension of indication application (EMA/VR/0000312495), the corresponding conclusion that no environmental risk is expected from the therapeutic use of enfortumab vedotin remains applicable.

## 2.2.3. Conclusion on the non-clinical aspects

Based on the updated data submitted in the application EMA/VR/0000312495, the extended indication does not lead to a significant increase in environmental exposure further to the use of enfortumab vedotin. Enfortumab vedotin is not expected to pose risk to the environment.

## 2.3.5. Discussion on clinical pharmacology

No new clinical pharmacology analyses beyond those conducted previously for enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab have been submitted, and no labeling revisions for the Clinical Pharmacology section of the EU SmPC for each respective approved product are proposed.

PK and immunogenicity of enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab from la/mUC studies EV-302 and EV-103, and from the MIBC study KEYNOTE-905, demonstrate that the administration of pembrolizumab in combination with enfortumab vedotin has no impact on the PK or immunogenicity of enfortumab vedotin

## 2.4. Clinical efficacy

## 2.4.1. Dose response study

No dose-response studies were submitted as part of this application. The dosing regimen of enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg (up to a maximum of 125 mg for patients ≥100 kg) on Days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle in combination with pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w used in KEYNOTE-B15 is consistent with the approved doses used in la/mUC and MIBC studies.

## Methods

## Study participants

Key inclusion criteria:

1. Histologically confirmed diagnosis of MIBC (clinical stage T2-T4aN0M0 or T1-T4aN1M0) with predominant (≥50%) urothelial histology confirmed by BICR (central pathology and imaging) and PD-L1 expression (CPS ≥10 or CPS &lt;10) confirmed by BICR (central pathology).
2. Clinically nonmetastatic bladder cancer (N≤1, M0) determined by imaging (CT or MRI of the chest/abdomen/pelvis), confirmed by BICR.
3. Deemed eligible for RC + PLND by a urologist and/or oncologist and agreed to undergo curative intent standard RC + PLND (including prostatectomy, if applicable) as per AUA/ASTRO/ASCO/SUO guidelines.
4. Transurethral resection of a bladder tumor (obtained within 60 days [+14 days] before enrolment [documented informed consent]) that was submitted for central pathology assessment and adequate to determine urothelial histology and PD-L1 expression.
5. Male or female, and at least 18 years of age, at the time of providing documented informed consent.
6. ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.

Key exclusion criteria:

- Known additional nonurothelial malignancy that was progressing or had required active anticancer treatment ≤3 years of study randomization.
- ≥N2 disease or metastatic disease (M1) as identified by imaging.
- Prior systemic treatment, chemoradiation, and/or radiation therapy for MIBC or NMIBC.
- o Prior treatment for NMIBC with intravesical instillation therapy such as BCG or

intravesical chemotherapy was permitted.

- Prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent or with an agent directed to another stimulatory or coinhibitory T-cell receptor (eg, CTLA-4, OX-40, CD137).
- Cisplatin-ineligible, as defined by meeting any 1 of the following criteria:
- o Impaired renal function with measured or calculated creatinine clearance &lt;60 mL/min
- o ECOG performance status ≥2
- o CTCAE v.5.0 Grade ≥2 peripheral neuropathy
- o CTCAE v 5.0 Grade ≥2 audiometric hearing loss
- o NYHA Class III or greater heart failure
- Prior radiotherapy to the bladder.
- Partial cystectomy of the bladder to remove any NMIBC or MIBC.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

- Has a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving chronic systemic steroid therapy (in dosing exceeding 10 mg daily of prednisone equivalent) or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior the first dose of study intervention. Inhaled or topical steroids are permitted in the absence of active autoimmune disease. Physiologic replacement (10 mg/day prednisone equivalent) doses of corticosteroids are permitted for participants with adrenal insufficiency.
- Has an active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in past 2 years (ie, with use of disease modifying agents, corticosteroids or immunosuppressive drugs). Replacement therapy (eg, thyroxine, insulin, or physiologic corticosteroid replacement therapy for adrenal, pituitary insufficiency, etc.) is not considered a form of systemic treatment and is allowed.

Additional details are available in the study protocol.

## Treatments

Patients were randomized 1:1 into one of the two arms to receive:

Arm A: 4 cycles of neoadjuvant EV + pembrolizumab, followed by RC + PLND, followed by 5 cycles of adjuvant EV + 13 cycles of adjuvant pembrolizumab.

Arm B: 4 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (gemcitabine + cisplatin), followed by RC+ PLND, followed by observation. For participants in Arm B at high risk of recurrence after RC + PLND, adjuvant nivolumab may be used per the approved product label, if locally available, and provided nivolumab is deemed appropriate for the participant by the investigator.

## Objectives Outcomes/endpoints

## Primary Objective

## Primary Endpoint

Objective: To compare EFS in Arm A (perioperative EV + pembrolizumab and RC + PLND) versus Arm B (neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin and RC + PLND)

Hypothesis (H1): Perioperative EV + pembrolizumab and RC + PLND (Arm A) will achieve superior EFS compared with neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin and RC + PLND (Arm B)

## Secondary Objectives

EFS, defined as the time from randomization to the first of the following events:

- -Radiographic disease progression precluding a curative intent surgery as assessed by BICR prior to RC + PLND
- -Failure to undergo surgery for participants with residual muscle-invasive disease and any radiographic disease present, biopsy proven MIBC will be considered an event regardless of radiographic findings
- -Gross residual disease left behind at time of surgery (surgeon unable to complete curative intent surgery due to unresectable tumor or newly discovered metastatic disease)
- -Local or distant recurrence post-RC + PLND as assessed by CT or MRI by BICR and/or biopsy. If biopsy is not feasible due to participant safety, CT/MRI alone will be sufficient
- -Death from any cause

NOTE: A non-urothelial second primary malignancy is not considered an event. Participants who develop high-risk NMIBC (in addition to muscle-invasive cancer) of the upper-tract/remaining urothelium after RC + PLND will be considered as having an event.

## Secondary Endpoints

Objective: To compare pCR rates obtained in Arm A (preoperative EV + pembrolizumab and RC + PLND) versus Arm B (neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin and RC + PLND)

Hypothesis (H2): Preoperative EV + pembrolizumab and RC + PLND (Arm A) will achieve superior pCR rates compared with neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin and RC + PLND (Arm B)

Objective: To compare the OS in Arm A (perioperative EV + pembrolizumab and RC + PLND) versus Arm B (neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin and RC + PLND)

pCR, defined as absence of viable tumor (pT0N0) in examined tissue from RC + PLND, as assessed by blinded central pathologic review

OS, defined as the time from randomization to death due to any cause

Study assessments:

All patients underwent baseline screening imaging (CT or MRI of the chest, abdomen, pelvis) for clinical staging, which was centrally evaluated using expedited imaging review by BICR, prior to randomization to confirm eligibility. Patients in both treatment arms completed 4 cycles of neoadjuvant study intervention,

followed by repeat imaging studies (same modality as screening) within ≤5 weeks (35 days +7 days) prior to the planned RC + PLND to exclude disease progression (confirmed by BICR), which might preclude curative intent surgery.

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Patients who remained radiographically free of distant metastases proceeded to surgery within 6 weeks of the last dose of neoadjuvant treatment. Patients might proceed to surgery outside of this period if the delays were due to an AE. Participants with surgery delays (beyond 12 weeks after the last dose of neoadjuvant treatment) for any reason, other than for an AE, may be considered with Sponsor consultation. Any occurrence of distant disease progression, per site-assessed imaging, at the pre-surgery timepoint (or during the neoadjuvant treatment phase) should be submitted as soon as possible to the iCRO for verification of progression by BICR. Radiographic disease progression precluding a curative intent surgery noted prior to RC + PLND (verified by BICR), failure to undergo surgery for patients with residual muscle invasive disease and any radiographic disease present (biopsy-proven MIBC will be considered an event regardless of radiographic findings), gross residual disease left behind at

time of surgery, local or distant recurrence as assessed radiographically by BICR and/or confirmed with biopsy (local pathology review), or death from any cause will be considered events and such patients will not receive further therapy on study but will transition into survival follow-up.

All RC + PLND surgical specimens (performed at main study site or another facility) were assessed by BICR pathology to determine pathologic response.

For patients who initially do not undergo RC + PLND within the protocol-specified window and subsequently undergo surgery at main study site or another facility, sites should collect and submit RC + PLND specimens for assessment by central pathology.

Following RC + PLND, all participants would have the post-surgery imaging at 6 weeks (±14 days), using the same imaging modality as at initial screening. Following the post-surgery baseline scan, imaging to be performed Q12W (±7 days) until end of Year 1 and 2 then; every 24 weeks in Year 3 and beyond.

## Biomarker assessment:

Patients enrolled in KEYNOTE-B15 were required to provide tumor tissue from a TUR specimen that was obtained up to 60 days (+14 days) prior to being enrolled into the study.

Tumor tissue was collected as either FFPE blocks (preferred) or unstained slides. The tissue that remained after conducting the clinical diagnosis of MIBC and PD-L1 CPS scoring was utilized for exploratory analyses such as Nectin-4 IHC.

PDL-1 (CPS ≥10 or CPS &lt;10) status was assessed by the blinded central pathology review. According to the protocol Individual participant PDL1 status will not be disclosed to investigative sites or study participants. PD-L1 22C3 IHC testing was done using Agilent PD-L1 22C3 IHC pharmDx (Agilent Technologies, Dako) at a central testing laboratory, which is CE marked and approved as a companion diagnostic to identify UC patients for treatment with pembrolizumab.

The Nectin-4 IHC assay was performed retrospectively on available samples of KEYNOTE-B15 from the 2 treatment groups. Fresh cut slides from FFPE blocks or slides that were within a 9-month stability window were tested, as established during the analytical validation process. A validated IHC assay (for research use only [RUO] using an anti-Nectin-4 antibody [clone M22-321b41.1]) was used to assess expression of Nectin-4 in FFPE tumor tissue at Q2 Solutions. The assay was previously used to assess Nectin-4 IHC expression in other EV clinical studies, including EV-302, KEYNOTE-905 and EV-103/KEYNOTE-869 studies. Nectin-4 staining was scored by pathologists trained on the Nectin-4 IHC assay. Nectin-4 expression was calculated by estimating the staining intensities of all tumor cells on the slide (3 = strong, 2 = moderate, 1 = low, 0 = negative) and the percentage of tumor cells that were positive at a particular intensity (PI-0, PI-1, PI-2, PI-3). An H-score ranging from 0 to 300 was derived for each tumor tissue sample using the equation:

H-score = (1 × PI-1) + (2 × PI-2) + (3 × PI-3).

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Nectin-4 IHC was reported on a continuous H-score scale ranging from 0 to 300; as such, no pathologist training was conducted around a validated specified cutoff value. Nectin-4 IHC H-scores of &lt;150, ≥150 to &lt;225, and ≥225 were used to define the subgroups.

## Sample size

The study enrolled 808 participants randomized in a 1:1 ratio.

For the EFS endpoint, based on a target number of 325 events at the final EFS analysis and 2 interim analyses at ~75% and 89% of the target number of events, the study has ~88.5% power to detect a HR of 0.7 at the allocated α=0.025 (1-sided).

Based on ~808 randomized participants, the power for the pCR rate endpoint at the α level of 0.001/0.025 (1-sided) is &gt;99% to detect a 22-percentage point difference between an underlying 28% pCR rate in the chemotherapy arm and a 50% pCR rate in the EV + pembrolizumab arm.

For the OS endpoint, based on a target number of 277 events and 3 interim analyses at ~51%, 70%, and 83% of the target number of events, the study has ~82.7%/83.1% power to detect a HR of 0.7 at the α level of 0.024/0.025 (1-sided).

Note that the above power calculations for EFS and OS are based on a constant hazard ratio assumption. The interim analysis timing and spending have been designed to ensure the final alpha available is maximized to make testing most sensitive when follow-up is available across both early and late parts of the survival and EFS distributions.

Based on the published studies, Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy plus Cystectomy Compared with Cystectomy Alone for Locally Advanced Bladder Cancer by H. Barton Grossman, et al [5] and Comparative Effectiveness of gemcitabine plus Cisplatin versus Methotrexate, Vinblastine, Doxorubicin, plus Cisplatin as Neoadjuvant Therapy for Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer by Galsky, et al [6], the above sample size and power calculations for EFS and OS assume the following:

- ∗ EFS follows an exponential distribution with a median of 43 months for the control group.
- ∗ OS follows an exponential distribution with a median of 66 months for the control group.
- ∗ Enrollment period of ~31 months
- ∗ An annual dropout rate of 10% for EFS and 1% for OS

## Randomisation

Intervention randomization will be stratified according to the following factors:

1. PD-L1 CPS ≥10 vs CPS &lt;10 (Note: if PD-L1 is not evaluable based on the submitted specimen, the participant will be assigned to the CPS &lt;10 group)
2. Tumor stage (T2N0 vs T3/T4aN0 vs T1-T4aN1)
3. Geographic regions (US vs EU vs MOW)

Note: PD-L1 status determined by the central vendor will not be disclosed to investigators and participants

## Blinding (masking)

The study is open labelled.

## Statistical methods

## Study population

The ITT population was planned to serve as the analysis population for EFS, pCR rate, pDS rate and OS and consists of all randomized participants whether or not treatment was administered. Participants in the ITT population were planned to be included in the treatment group to which they are randomized.

## Primary endpoint, estimand and analysis

EFS was planned as the primary endpoint for the study. No estimand was defined in the study although a definition was provided post hoc. Briefly, the primary estimand is intended to contrast the effect of perioperative EV + pembrolizumab relative to neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin using a treatment policy strategy, under which endpoints are assessed regardless of the occurrence of intercurrent events. Three IEs of interest were defined as IE1) discontinuation of perioperative EV + pembrolizumab or neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin, IE2) use of new anticancer therapy, and IE3) failure to undergo surgery. IE1 and IE2 were handled via treatment policy strategy, while IE3 (failure to undergo surgery) was handled via \"Treatment policy strategy (adjusted) - * Participants who did not undergo surgery and had not experienced an EFS event were censored at the last disease assessment within 16 weeks after last dose of neoadjuvant treatment or randomization.\"

The non-parametric Kaplan-Meier method was planned to be used to estimate the EFS curve in each treatment group. The treatment difference in EFS was planned to be assessed by the stratified log-rank test. A stratified Cox proportional hazard model with a single treatment covariate and Efron's method of tie handling was planned to be used to assess the magnitude of the treatment difference (ie, HR) between the treatment arms. The HR and its 95% CI from the stratified Cox model with a single covariate of treatment arm was planned to be reported.

Participants who refuse or are unable to undergo RC without a protocol-defined event were planned to be censored at the last disease assessment within 16 weeks of last dose of neoadjuvant treatment (or within 16 weeks of the randomization date for participants who do not receive any treatment).

Participants who refuse or are unable to undergo surgery and who develop a protocol-defined event at any time were planned to be counted as events. Participants who refuse or are unable to undergo surgery, but without a post-screening scan were planned to be censored at Day 1 from randomization.

## Sensitivity analyses

Since disease assessment is performed periodically, events such as progression and recurrence can occur any time in the time interval between the last assessment where the event was not documented and the assessment when the event is documented. In order to evaluate the robustness of the EFS endpoint, a sensitivity analysis with a different set of censoring rules was

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

considered. The sensitivity analysis was planned as the same as the primary analysis except that events after 2 consecutive missed disease assessments or after new anticancer therapy if any should be censored at last disease assessment prior to the earlier date of ≥2 consecutive missed disease assessments and new anticancer therapy.

## Key secondary endpoints and estimands

pCR (pathological Complete Response) rates (pCRR) and OS were planned as key secondary endpoints for the study.

The stratified Miettinen and Nurminen method with strata weighting by sample size was planned to be used for the comparison of pCR rates between treatment arms. The difference in pCR rates, its 95% CI, and the corresponding p-value from the stratified Miettinen and Nurminen method with strata weighting by sample size were planned to be reported.

Participants who are discontinued from the study intervention and continue with other treatment not specified by the study prior to definitive surgery will be classified as not having a pCR (nonresponders) in the efficacy analyses, regardless of the results obtained from the surgery. Participants who refuse or are unable to undergo surgery and participants with relevant data missing are considered non-responders. For participants who refuse or are unable to undergo surgery and achieve cCR (per Protocol Section 8.2.3), sensitivity analyses may be conducted in which 1) participants with cCR are excluded from the pCR analysis, or 2) participants with cCR are considered responders.

OS was planned to be analysed as EFS. The stratification factors used for randomization were planned to be applied to both the stratified log-rank test and the stratified Cox model. Participants without documented death at the time of analysis were planned to be censored at the date the participant was last known to be alive.

## Subgroup analyses

The following subgroup analyses were prespecified:

- PD-L1 CPS (&lt;10, ≥10)
- Disease stage (T2N0, T3/T4aN0, T1-T4aN1)
- Geographic region (US, EU, MOW)
- Age category (&lt;65 years, ≥65 years)
- Sex (female, male)
- Race (white, all others)
- Smoking status (never, former, current)

## Interim and multiplicity for primary and key-secondary endpoints

Three interim analyses are planned in addition to the final analysis for this study. All randomized participants will be included. Results of the interim analyses will be reviewed by the DMC. Details of the boundaries for establishing statistical significance with regard to efficacy are presented under \"Multiplicity\".

If EFS was significant at any IA, then the next IA(s) was planned to be triggered by OS events. If the OS event accrual is much slower than expected and the final targeted number of events cannot be reached by the end of year 6 after last participant randomized, then the final OS analysis may be performed at the end of year 6 after last participant randomized at the latest.

pCR

The study was planned to test pCR rate (H2) only when EFS is significant. The test statistics of pCR rate was planned to be computed at IA1. If superiority for EFS is declared at IA2 or later, the test statistic previously computed at IA1 for H2 was planned to be used for inferential testing. Note that if superiority is achieved for the EFS hypothesis, α was planned to be rolled over to the pCR rate hypothesis and the pCR rate hypothesis was planned to be tested with an α level of 0.001. If superiority is achieved for both the EFS and OS hypotheses, α=0.024 was planned to be rolled over to the hypothesis for pCR rate and the pCR rate hypothesis was planned to be tested with an updated alpha level of 0.025.

OS

The study was planned to test OS (H3) at IA1, IA2, IA3 and FA. There is no alpha initially allocated to test OS. Note that if superiority is achieved for the EFS hypothesis only, α was planned to be rolled over to the OS hypothesis and the OS hypothesis was planned to be tested with an α level of 0.024. If superiority is achieved for both the pCR rate and EFS hypotheses, α was planned to be rolled over to the OS hypothesis and the OS hypothesis was planned to be tested with an α level of 0.025. Possible αlevels were derived using a Lan-DeMets spending function approximating O'BrienFleming bounds. ## Conduct of the study

## Protocol amendments

Table 10. Protocol Amendments for KEYNOTE-B15

| Document           | Date of Issue   | Overall Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Amendment 05       | 11-DEC-2024     | To revise the statistical analysis plan to ensure sufficient follow-up time for EFS and OS analyses based on a recently published study in the same patient population.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Amendment 04       | 17-NOV-2023     | To allow collection of late-onset peripheral neuropathy data to fulfill an FDA postmarketing requirement for EV, and to ensure consistency between the definition of EFS in the primary endpoint and the statistical analysis plan for this endpoint.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Amendment 03       | 06-FEB-2023     | pCR is revised to a key secondary endpoint and EFS is the only primary endpoint. As a result, the multiplicity strategy is updated to allocate all initial alpha to EFS to test the EFS endpoint more robustly. In addition, adjuvant nivolumab is permitted in Arm B when clinically indicated and per the label, dose modification recommendations for pneumonitis/ILD related to enfortumab vedotin were added, changes were made to align with the EU CTR, and other minor updates and clarifications were made. |
| Amendment 02       | 04-APR-2022     | Added additional guidance on management of certain Grade 2 skin reactions and any grade bullous lesions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Amendment 01       | 14-MAY-2021     | Added updated dose modification and supportive care guidelines for rash related to enfortumab vedotin, harmonized the presentation of safety information across all FDA-approved PD-1/L1 antibody prescribing information, made additional minor changes throughout the protocol, and updated the SAP.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [Original Protoco] | 04-NOV-2020     | Not applicable                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

EFS=event-free survival; EU CTR=European Union Clinical Trials Regulation; EV=enfortumab vedotin; FDA=Food and Drug Administration; ILD=interstitial lung disease; OS=overall survival; pCR=pathological complete response; PD-L1=programmed cell death ligand 1; SAP=statistical analysis plan.

Source: [16.1.1]

In Amendment 03 (dated 06-FEB-2023), pCR was downgraded from primary to key secondary endpoint. In initial protocol versions, an alpha of 0.001 was attributed to pCR, while 0.024 was attributed to EFS.

In Amendment 05 (dated 11-DEC-2024), follow-up time for EFS and OS was updated (based on the NIAGARA publication) and the sample size was updated from 784 to 808 participants (while maintaining 325 events) to reflect the actual enrolment. Timings and power of IA were adjusted,

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

and one additional OS IA was added. Furthermore, the original primary pCR analysis was moved to sensitivity analysis.

## Protocol deviations

Important (i.e. those that may significantly impact the quality or integrity of key study data or that may significantly affect a participant's rights, safety, or well-being) were reported for 47 (11.6%) participants in the EV + pembrolizumab group and 38 (9.4%) participants in the cis + gem group. None was considered clinically important and none was classified as a serious GCP compliance issue.

There were 3 protocol-defined overdoses (2 overdoses of enfortumab vedotin and 1 overdose of gemcitabine). None were associated with AEs.

Protocol deviations associated with the COVID-19 pandemic were reported for 11 (2.7%) participants in the EV + pembrolizumab group and 16 (4%) participants in the cis + gem group.

## Overall Survival

Since the EFS null hypothesis was rejected, OS was formally tested at IA1 with the multiplicity adjusted p-value boundary of 0.0038.

## Patient-reported outcomes

Three PRO questionnaires were used: EORTC QLQ-C30, BCI and EQ-5D-5L VAS.

The baseline PRO assessment was defined as the neoadjuvant Cycle 1 assessment. The mean change from baseline to post-surgery Week 42 was evaluated. Post-surgery Week 42 was the latest time point at which the completion rate was ~60% and the compliance rate was ~80%

based on the blinded data review prior to database lock for any PRO analysis. points deterioration for EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/QoL score from baseline) with

Definitive TTD was defined as the time from baseline to the first onset of deterioration (e.g., ≥10 confirmation deterioration at all subsequent timepoints.

No clinically meaningful differences in HRQoL were observed between perioperative EV + pembrolizumab compared with cis + gem with respect to:

- EORTC QLQ-C30 (global health status/QoL [Items 29 and 30]), physical functioning, and role functioning
- BCI: urinary, bowel, and sexual domains
- EQ-5D-5L VAS

## Exploratory analysis by Nectin-4

An exploratory analysis was conducted to assess the distribution of Nectin-4 expression in tissue samples collected in KEYNOTE-B15 to further investigate the relationship of Nectin-4 expression with outcomes with perioperative enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab compared with neoadjuvant cisplatin + gemcitabine.

The Nectin-4 IHC assay was performed retrospectively on available samples, using a validated IHC assay (for research use only [RUO] using an anti-Nectin-4 antibody [clone M22-321b41.1]) in FFPE tumor tissue at Q2 Solutions. Nectin-4 expression was calculated by estimating the staining intensities of all tumor cells on the slide and the percentage of tumor cells that were positive at a particular intensity, deriving a continuous H-score scale ranging from 0 to 300. The exploratory cutoff H-score values for subgroup analysis were: &lt;150, 150 to &lt;225, ≥225.

## 2.4.3. Discussion on clinical efficacy

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

The scope of this variation is to support the extension of indication of enfortumab vedotin in combination with Keytruda for the perioperative treatment of resectable muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) in adults eligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy, based on the results from the pivotal trial KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304.

## Design and conduct of clinical studies

KEYNOTE-B15/ EV-304 is an ongoing Phase 3, randomized, active-controlled, parallel-group, multisite, open-label study comparing perioperative enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab with neoadjuvant cisplatin + gemcitabine in participants with muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and with cT2-T4aN0M0 or cT1-T4aN1M0. All patients should have been eligible to cisplatin, thus the experimental combination has been compared to 4 cycles of neoadjuvant cisplatin + gemcitabine given before radical surgery. In the control arm, participants initially received no adjuvant therapy, although adjuvant nivolumab was allowed if deemed appropriate by the investigator after protocol Amendment 3, implemented one year after starting enrolment due to the approval of such treatment. The control treatment is deemed overall appropriate. Adjuvant nivolumab was used only in 25 patients in the control arm, therefore it is not possible to have a robust characterisation of the specific contribution of adjuvant nivolumab to EFS in the target population, nor to conclude regarding the benefit of perioperative EV + pembrolizumab relative to the current adjuvant standard of care.

The study was open-label; the primary endpoint of event-free survival (EFS) was based on blinded independent central review (BICR) assessment, which is appropriated in an open-label setting to support the objectivity of the primary endpoint evaluation The EFS definition is considered acceptable from a clinical perspective. EFS definition was clarified with Amendments 04 and 05 specifying that, in case of failure to undergo surgery, biopsy proven MIBC was considered an event regardless of radiographic findings. Biopsy confirmation was systematically required to evaluate residual muscle invasive disease in the bladder, and this clarification did not result in the reclassification of EFS events relative to prior versions of the protocol.

In Amendment 3, pCR was downgraded from primary to key secondary endpoint. This is clinically acceptable, as relationship with long-term outcomes such as EFS and OS has not been sufficiently validated in MIBC, further pCR is relevant only for the neoadjuvant part of the treatment.

Overall, the methods have been chosen appropriately with respect to the study objectives, and modifications introduced during the duration of the study were appropriately justified and are not considered critical.

Survival endpoints(RFS and OS) were planned to be analysed using Kaplan-Maier curves and logrank test, while pCR was planned to be analysed using the Miettinen and Nurmien method. This is in principle agreeable. However, overlapping/crossing of the EFS and OS curves was observed within the first six months; in the same time frame, a high number of censoring events was observed. The early censoring was justified according to the censoring rules for participants who did not undergo surgery and did not experience an event and is further discussed below. A requested restricted mean survival time (RMST) analysis was conducted for both EFS and OS. The analysis consistently showed that, while the EFS curves separate early (Month 12) and decisively, the separation for OS doesn't happen until much later (Month 30) and remains numerically modest. This is aligned with the results of the primary analyses.

No estimands were originally defined in the trial, although the primary estimand for EFS was provided post-hoc during the assessment. Several scenarios for participants who did not undergo surgery (\"refused or were unable to\") were presented, including for scenarios in which the

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

neoadjuvant therapy successfully reduced the tumor (\"No MIBC, no locally advanced diseased, no distant PD or no death, whether or not new anticancer therapy is initiated\"). Participants undergoing this scenario were \"Censored at last disease assessment within 16 weeks of last dose of neoadjuvant treatment (or within 16 weeks of randomization for participants who do not receive any treatment)\". The rationale for the 16 weeks was clarified by the MAH, i.e. to avoid attributing favorable long-term outcomes to participants who may have declined surgery due to an absence of detectable disease following neoadjuvant treatment (the 16-week window reflects the time when participants would have had surgery). Additional sensitivity analyses confirmed the results of the study.

Three interim analyses (IAs) and one final analysis (FA) were planned. Each IA was scheduled to take place only after at least 75% of the expected EFS events had occurred, all participants had the opportunity to undergo RC+PLND, and the last participant had been randomized for a minimum of 18 months. These requirements ensured sufficient maturity of the EFS data at each analysis and minimized the risk that the interim results could influence the conduct or design of the ongoing study. Statistical boundaries were established using a Lan-DeMets alpha-spending function and were adjusted according to the observed information fraction, which is considered appropriate.

The study underwent five protocol amendments. The most substantial amendment, where study design and SAP were adjusted was amendment 3 (reported above). In Amendment 05, the MAH states that follow-up time was increased; this increase was due to a slower than expected accrual time and impacted on the timing of the EFS and OS analyses, but not on the number of events needed for each IA and FA. Overall, the protocol amendments are acceptable and should not affect the study integrity and reliability of the results. There were several important protocol deviations, which were fairly balanced between the arms [in 47 (11.6%) vs. 38 (9.4%) patients in arms A and B, respectively] and mostly related to a safety event not being reported per the timelines outlined in the protocol. The important protocol deviations related to COVID-19 pandemic were infrequent in both treatment arms of the KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304. The number and character of the important protocol deviations do not give rise to concerns about a potential impact on the study data.

Baseline characteristics: A total of 1225 patients were screened and 808 randomized in the experimental (n=405) and control (n=403) arm, stratified by region, stage and PD-L1 status.

The demographic and clinical characteristics of the patients at baseline were generally balanced in both arms of study KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304 and are considered representative of the overall patient population with resectable MIBC eligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy in Europe. The median age was 66 years, with range of 35 to 83. The majority of patient were men (81%), white (77%) and had an ECOG performance status of 0 (77.6%). Tumours expressing PD-L1 with a CPS ≥10 were observed in 57.3% of patients. Most patients had T3/T4aN0 disease (72.5%), while 8.2% had T1-4aN1 disease. \"Pure\" urothelial carcinoma histology was present in 89.5% of tumours. Patients were primarily enrolled in the EU (50.9%) and most of the world (34.5%), with 14.6% enrolled in the US.

Patient's disposition and study conduct.

Most of the patients who started neoadjuvant treatment completed the planned 4 cycles (85.4% vs 88.9%), although there were more discontinuations in the experimental arm due to adverse event (12.2% in the EV + pembrolizumab group and 7.8% in the cis + gem group). Overall, few less patients (351 vs 361) participants in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group vs in the cis + gem group underwent surgery (including 2 participants who did not receive neoadjuvant study medication), while more patients did not undergo surgery after neoadjuvant treatment (52 vs 37 participants, 13% vs 9%), in the experimental arm. The analysis of detailed reasons for not

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

undergoing surgery did not suggest bias due to the open-label design in terms of physician/patient's decision. Compared with the control arm, fewer patients in the experimental arm did not proceed to surgery due to disease progression (11.1% vs 14.3%). However, more patients did not proceed to surgery due to AE (24.1% vs 14.3%), confirming the toxicity of the EV + pembrolizumab combination. Surgical resection was complete in almost all patients, and the type of surgical procedure was similar in both treatment arms. Surgery was more frequently delayed due to AE in the pembrolizumab + EV arm, however the median time from randomization to surgery and from the end of neoadjuvant treatment to surgery was comparable between arms.

In the pembrolizumab +EV arm, 262 out of 351 patients (i.e. 75% of the total) who underwent surgery received adjuvant treatment. The remaining 89 patients (25%) did not proceed to adjuvant treatment (89/351), being adverse event, the most common reason followed by participant's withdrawal. Most of the patients starting adjuvant treatment were however able to complete the planned treatment with AE again the most common reason for discontinuation (13%). Overall, data reflects the toxicity of the combination and the need for careful patient selection, as the perioperative EV+pembro regimen appears to be more toxic (higher rates of discontinuation due to AE at any study phase; see safety discussion) than neoadjuvant cis+gem followed by surgery.

Regarding post-study treatments, more patients received following therapies considering all settings in the control arm, as expected (15.8% vs 31.8%).

## Efficacy data and additional analyses

Primary endpoint: At the IA1, median survival follow-up was 30.8 months (range 0.5, 53.6). No patients were still under active treatment. At this timepoint, EFS events occurred in 21.5% vs 36.2% of the population in the experimental vs control arm. The study demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in EFS by BICR: HR 0.53, 95%CI 0.41, 0.70, p&lt;0.0001. KM curves were almost overlapping during the first 6 months including several censorings in both arms, then started to separate: the improvement in EFS rate is approximately 10% at month 12 (86% vs 75.4%), and 13% at month 18 (82.2 vs 68.8%), and is maintained long-term, acknowledging that curves are still highly censored afterwards. Median EFS is reached only in the control arm, but this data is not yet interpretable. Pre-specified EFS sensitivity analyses and EFS by investigator assessment were consistent with the primary EFS analysis by BICR.

Secondary endpoints: since the EFS null hypothesis was rejected, OS was formally tested at IA1 showing a statistically significant survival advantage for the perioperiative pembrolizumab + EV vs neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy. With 17% vs 24.6% of OS events, HR was 0.65 (95%CI 0.48, 0.89), p=0.0029. KM curves separated after month 6 and remained separated afterwards, although highly censored from month 20. Medians were not reached in either arm, but approximately 5% increase in OS rate is observed (i.e. OS rate at month 12: 93.1% vs 89.6%; OS rate at 18 months 89.4% vs 84.5%). In the initial part of the OS curve however, more deaths were observed in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group compared with the cis + gem group (8 vs 4) during the first 5 months post-randomization. However, the small numbers of death events in this timeframe precludes to draw definitive conclusions about the possible risk factors of early deaths in the pembrolizumab + EV arm. The interim OS results are considered promising; however their interpretation is limited by the low data maturity (~21%). Thefinal OS results are expected to be submitted post-authorization to further characterise the efficacyin this early setting (REC).

pCR was also formally tested per multiplicity strategy, showing a statistically significant 23.4% (95%CI 16.7-29.8, p&lt;0.0001) improvement for pembrolizumab+EV over standard cis+gem

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

(55.8% vs 32.5%). The absolute pCR rate was similar to the pCR of 57.1% achieved after neoadjuvant pembrolizumab+EV in the cisplatin-ineligible population of KEYNOTE-905 (EMA/VR/0000312515). Consistently, pathological downstaging was in favour of the pembrolizumab+EV neoadjuvant treatment (63.7% vs 45.2%).

DFS based on BICR evaluating the risk of local or distant recurrence or death in patients who were disease free after surgery (339 vs 330) was also in favour of the pembrolizumab+EV arm (HR 0.50 (95% CI: 0.36, 0.70), thus supporting the overall result.

The patient-reported outcomes did not suggest meaningful differences in the endpoints analysed.

A prespecified exploratory analysis of EFS by pCR outcome was provided, however, as this is based on post-randomization outcomes, the results need to be interpreted with caution.

Subgroup analyses: subgroup analyses suggested consistent benefit of perioperative pembrolizumab + EV vs neoadjuvant cis-gem across prespecified subgroups. In patients with lower disease stage T2N0 and expected better prognosis (19.3% of the ITT population), the advantage in EFS and OS appears more limited [OS HR 0.87 (0.37, 2.06); EFS HR 0.76 (0.39, 1.51)] compared to higher disease stages, however T2N0 subgroup is small with few OS events occurring: considering that HRs are &lt;1, and CIs are large, the overall data do not justify an exclusion of those patients from the indication. Results of subgroup analyses are included in the EPAR.

Regarding molecular biomarkers, consistent results are observed in patients with PD-L1 expression CPS &lt;10 and CPS≥10. Results in the CPS&lt;1 subgroup need to be interpreted with caution due to the exploratory nature of the analysis, the small sample size of this subset (32 vs 30) and the lack of a clear trend in all endpoints.

The potential significance of Nectin-4 expression was evaluated as an exploratory endpoint using leftover tissue samples from 638 out of 808 patients, following assessment of PDL-1 expression and histological confirmation. The mean Nectin-4 H score was 233 (SD 68.2) across both treatment arms, and most patients had a score of 225 or higher, although there was an imbalance between the two treatment arms. The results showed that Nectin-4 expression did not impact EFS, OS, or the ability to achieve a pathological complete response, suggesting no correlation between Nectin-4 expression and the likelihood of responding to perioperative treatment with EV+pembro.

Contribution of components (CoC): The study design does not allow to formally evaluate the contribution of each component (EV and pembrolizumab) of the combination, as well as the contribution of each phase of treatment (neoadjuvant and adjuvant). Nonetheless, the combination of EV and pembrolizumab from the metastatic setting and the clear superiority of the combination shown in KEYNOTE-B15 study attenuates the concern around the individual contribution of each component.

## Wording of indication

Patients had to be deemed resectable to be included in the protocol and thus the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab regime should not be indicated for downsizing an unresectable tumour. The finally agreed indication wording was updated to reflect resectable MIBC.

During the procedure, the indication for muscle-invasive bladder cancer was editorially revised to refer to adults with muscle-invasive bladder cancer irrespective of cisplatin eligibility, reflecting the combined evidence from KEYNOTE-905 (cisplatin-ineligible patients; EC-approved under EMA/VR/0000312515) and KEYNOTE-B15 (cisplatin-eligible patients; the current procedure). This revision consolidated the cisplatin-ineligible population and the cisplatin-eligible population into a

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

single cisplatin agnostic indication. The distinction between the two indications (cisplatin ineligible vs eligible) is maintained in the instructions for duration of therapy in section 4.2 of the SmPC since there is a difference in the number of neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment cycles for the two indications (cisplatin-ineligible vs cisplatin-eligible) based on the two pivotal studies KEYNOTE-905 and KEYNOTE-B15. Furthermore, these studies are discussed separately in section 5.1. In conclusion, the proposed wording of the indication is acceptable.

The final agreed indication wording was updated as:

Padcev, in combination with pembrolizumab, as neoadjuvant treatment and then continued after radical cystectomy as adjuvant treatment, is indicated for the treatment of adults with resectable muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC).

## 2.4.4. Conclusions on the clinical efficacy

The KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304 study met its primary and key secondary endpoints, showing a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in EFS and OS with perioperative enfortumab-vedotin in combination with pembrolizumab, administered as neoadjuvant treatment followed by adjuvant treatment after radical cystectomy in patients with resectable MIBC, who are eligible for neoadjuvant cisplatin.

Although the results are based on the first interim analysis, more mature data are not considered needed for the present assessment, however as this is an early curative setting, final OS study results are expected to be submitted post-approval to further characterise the efficacy (REC).

## 2.5. Clinical safety

## Introduction

The safety evaluation of neoadjuvant and adjuvant EV + pembrolizumab in patients with cisplatineligible MIBC is based on data from the KEYNOTE-B15 study. Safety analyses were conducted using the APaT population, which included all randomized participants who received at least 1 dose of study treatment as of the DCO 27-OCT-2025 and were analyzed according to the study treatment that they received.

## Patient exposure

At DCO (27-OCT-2025) 403 participants received at least 1 dose of perioperative EV + pembrolizumab and 396 participants received at least 1 dose of cis + gem in KEYNOTE-B15. The last dose of study treatment was administered on 08-MAY-2025, thus all participants were off study treatment at the time of DCO.

The dosing regimen in KEYNOTE-B15 was as follows:

Treatment Arm 1: Neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg on Days 1 and 8 q3w for 4 cycles + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w for 4 cycles + RC + PLND + adjuvant enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg on Days 1 and 8 q3w for 5 cycles + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w for 13 cycles

Treatment Arm 2: Neoadjuvant cisplatin 70 mg/m2 on Day 1 q3w for 4 cycles + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on Days 1 and 8 + RC + PLND

For KN-B15, treatment includes study medications and surgery.

For KN-B15, EV + Pembro Combo ISD, and Pembro Mono RSD, non-serious adverse events up to 30 days of last treatment and serious adverse events up to 90 days of last treatment are included.

For EV Mono ISD, non-serious adverse events and serious adverse events up to 30 days of the last treatment are included.

For Pembro and EV+Pembro studies, MedDRA preferred terms \"Neoplasm Progression\", \"Malignant Neoplasm Progression\" and \"Disease Progression\" not related to the drug are excluded.

For KN-B15, grades are based on NCI CTCAE version 5.0.

Database cutoff date for KN-B15: 27OCT2025.

The list of studies and database cutoff dates for the aggregate safety datasets within this table are provided in the appendix of Module 2.7.4.

For KN-B15, treatment includes study medications and surgery.

For KN-B1 5 and EV + Pembro Combo ISD, non-serious adverse events up to 30 days of last treatment and serious adverse events up to 90 days of last treatment are included.

Database cutoff date for KN-B15: 27OCT2025.

Cutaneous rash was the most frequent skin reaction reported (EV+ Pembro: 61.8%, Ev+ Pembro combo ISD 65.2%, EV Mono ISD 52.3%), while severe reactions were registered in the 19.4% of the EV+ Pembro arm: conjunctivitis (5.5%) and skin exfoliation (3%) were the most frequently reported severe skin reactions. Four cases of Steven Johnson syndrome (1%) and 6 of dermatitis bullous (1.5%) were included in the skin severe reaction PT. In the reference datasets, the reported rates of severe cutaneous skin reactions were 28.5% in the EV+ Pembro ISD and 25.1% in the EV Mono ISD.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Clinical AEs of skin hyperpigmentation include skin discoloration, skin hyperpigmentation, and pigmentation disorder. The percentage of participants with skin hyperpigmentation was 3.5% in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group, with no events reported in the cis + gem group. The percentage of participants with skin hyperpigmentation observed in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group (3.5%) was similar to that of the EV + pembrolizumab ISD (6.9%) and EV mono ISD (10.0%). All AEs of skin hyperpigmentation were Grade ≤2 events and nonserious across all the analyzed groups.

## Hyperglycemia

Hyperglicemia was recorded in 19.6% of subjects in the EV+Pembro arm; overall rate of hyperglycemia resulted similar to the Pembro-EV (19.9%) and mono EV ISDs (16.8%). Most of the reported cases were grade 1-2, accounting for the 12.9% of the events and were mostly represented by transient hyperglycemia. When incidence was adjusted for exposure, it resulted similar to what reported in the EV+ Pembro ISD and mono EV ISD (2.47, 2.62 and 4.19 respectively).

## Infusion-Related Reactions

The percentage of participants with IRR events was similar in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group (2.5%) compared with the cis + gem group (4.5%), the EV + pembrolizumab ISD (3.9%) and the EV mono ISD (6.3%); all AEs were ≤Grade 3 and nonserious for participants in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group. No IRR events in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab led to dose reductions or discontinuation of any study drug or enfortumab vedotin.

## ILD/pneumonitis

The mechanism for enfortumab vedotin-induced pneumonitis is not known; pneumonitis/ILD events are considered an important identified risk for both pembrolizumab and enfortumab vedotin.

For KN-B15, treatment includes study medications and surgery.

For KN-B15, EV + Pembro Combo ISD, and Pembro Mono RSD, non-serious adverse events up to 30 days of last treatment and serious adverse events up to 90 days of last treatment are included. Database cutoff date for KN-B15: 27OCT2025.

The list of studies and database cutoff dates for the aggregate safety datasets within this table are provided in the appendix of Module 2.7.4.

In the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group, 4 G-4 events (3 cases of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and 1 of dermatitis bullous) were reported; the median time to onset of first AEOSI of severe skin reaction in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group, EV + pembrolizumab ISD, and pembrolizumab RSD were 12.0 days, 79.0 days, and 85.0 days, respectively. At DCO, events for most participants with severe skin reactions (58/69 [84.1%]) were considered resolved. Severe skin reactions led to discontinuation of any study drug, enfortumab vedotin, and pembrolizumab for 5.5%, 5.0%, and 3.2%, respectively.

A specific adverse event appears on this report only if its incidence in one or more of the columns meets the incidence criterion in the report title, after rounding.

Treatment includes preoperative study medications and surgery.

Preoperative/surgical phase starts the date when the first treatment is administered and continues until the date the first postoperative study medications are administered.

Included adverse events in the preoperative/surgical phase. If there are no postoperative study medications, nonserious adverse events up to 30 days of last treatment and serious adverse events up to 90 days of last treatment are included.

MedDRA V28.1 preferred terms \"Neoplasm progression\", \"Malignant neoplasm progression\" and \"Disease progression\" not related to the drug are excluded.

Database Cutoff Date: 27OCT2025.

Drug-related AEs, as assessed by the investigator, were similar in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group (93.8%) and the cis + gem group (93.9%). The most frequently reported drug-related AEs within each group (incidence ≥20%) were:

- Perioperative EV + pembrolizumab: pruritus (38.7%), alopecia (27.8%), rash (20.8%), and dysgeusia (20.1%)
- Cis + gem: neutropenia (54.0%), anemia (45.7%), nausea (43.2%), thrombocytopenia (26.5%), and fatigue (25.3%).

In general, these drug-related AEs were primarily Grade 1 or 2.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Grade 3- 5 AEs were reported in the 37.2% of the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group and 46.5% in the cis + gem group (46.5%).

- Perioperative EV + pembrolizumab: neutropenia (6.2%), rash maculopapular (4.0%), rash (3.5%), and ALT increased, hyperglycemia, and pruritus (2.5% each)
- Cis + gem: neutropenia (32.3%), anemia (11.1%), thrombocytopenia (8.3%), and leukopenia (4.0%)

## Adverse Events Leading to Surgery Delay or Cancellation

The median time from randomization to surgery in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group was 15.7 weeks (range: 6.0 to 55.1 weeks) and 15.9 weeks (range: 7.6 to 73.1 weeks) in the cis + gem group. The median time from last dose of neoadjuvant treatment to surgery was 5.4 weeks (range: 1.0 to 44.0 weeks) in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group and 5.3 weeks (range: 1.4 to 63.9 weeks) in the cis + gem group.

A delay in the undergoing surgery was defined as time from last neoadjuvant treatment to surgery [or time from randomization to surgery if no neoadjuvant treatment received] &gt;8 weeks; it was registered in the 16.8% in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group and 14.4% in the cis + gem group.

## AESI during the Preoperative/Surgical phase

Skin reactions: 62.0% in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group and 12.9% in the cis + gem group. Serious skin reactions were reported for 5.5% of participants.

Peripheral neuropathy: 34.2% in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group and 11.4% in the cis + gem group. Sensory (32.8%) were more common than motor events (3.0%); Serious events of peripheral neuropathy were reported for 1 participant (0.2%).

Hyperglycemia: 16.6% in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group and 7.3% in the cis + gem group. Serious events of hyperglycemia were reported for 1.5% of participants

Ocular disorders: 23.6% in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group and 3.5% in the cis + gem group. There were no participants with serious ocular disorders.

IRR: 1.2% in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group and 4.5% in the cis + gem group. There were no serious IRR events.

## Adverse Events in the Surgical Phase and Surgical Mortality

Surgical Phase was defined as the period from the time of surgery until 30/90 days after surgery for nonserious AEs/SAEs, or until the start of adjuvant study medication (applicable for the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group only).

The median time to onset of the first Grade 3 to 5 AE for the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group in the Postoperative Phase was 74.0 days (range: 1 to 362 days). Drug-related 3-5 AEs were reported in the 21.4%, in absence of events reported with incidence ≥2%. SAE: 35.1% of participants experienced SAEs. The most frequently reported SAEs (incidence ≥2%) in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group were UTI (8.0%) and sepsis (2.7%). SAE considered drugrelated were described in the 11.8% of participants in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab; No drug-related SAEs were reported with frequency ≥2%. No deaths due to AEs in the Postoperative Phase were assessed as drug-related by the Investigator.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Adverse Events Resulting in Treatment Discontinuation in the postoperative phase

Overall, 28.6%, 21.8%, and 13.7% of participants in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group experienced AEs resulting in discontinuation of any study drug, discontinuation of pembrolizumab, and discontinuation of enfortumab vedotin, respectively.

AEs resulting in discontinuation of any study drug and pembrolizumab for ≥2% of participants were diarrhea and pneumonitis (2.3% each), respectively. All AEs resulting in discontinuation of enfortumab vedotin occurred in &lt;2% of participants.

Diarrhoea and pneumonitis were identified as the commonly reported drug-related AEs leading to any drug discontinuation for pembrolizumab, while peripheral neuropathy was the most common reported in the EV (1.1%).

## Adverse Events Resulting in Treatment Interruption in the postoperative phase

Overall, 43.9%, 37.4%, and 29.8% of participants in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group experienced AEs resulting in interruption of any study drug, interruption of pembrolizumab, and interruption of enfortumab vedotin, respectively. AEs resulting in interruption of any study drug, interruption of pembrolizumab, and interruption of enfortumab vedotin for ≥2% of participants in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group were:

- Any drug: diarrhea (6.5%), UTI (6.1%), COVID-19 (2.7%), and pyrexia (2.3%)
- Pembrolizumab: diarrhea (5.3%), UTI (5.0%), and COVID-19 (2.3%)
- Enfortumab vedotin: UTI (4.6%), diarrhea (4.2%), and COVID-19 (2.3%)

Diarrhea was the most common reported Drug-related AEs resulting in interruption in the any study drug, pembrolizumab (4.6% each), and enfortumab vedotin (3.1%).

## Adverse Events Resulting in Dose reduction in the postoperative phase

In the Postoperative Phase, 4.6% of participants in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group experienced AEs resulting in dose reduction of enfortumab vedotin. All AEs resulting in dose reduction of enfortumab vedotin occurred in &lt;1% of participants.

## Haematology

See sections on AESIs anaemia and neutropenia.

## Clinical chemistry

Laboratory abnormalities were generally consistent with the EV + pembrolizumab ISD and individual safety datasets of enfortumab vedotin monotherapy and pembrolizumab monotherapy. There were no specific trends in laboratory abnormalities in the perioperative EV +pembrolizumab group that suggest any new safety concern. See also section on AESI hyperglycemia.

## Safety related to drug-drug interactions and other interactions

No new data on drug-drug interactions were submitted with this variation. As per the SmPC, no formal drug-drug interaction studies with EV have been conducted.
