The overall rates of drug related AEs leading to any drug discontinuation was 35.2% in the EV+Pembro, 11.1% in the cis-gem, 44.7% in the EV+Pembro ISD, 21.2% in the EV Mono ISD and 14% in the Pembro mono RSD.

## Adverse Events Resulting in Any Drug Interruption by System Organ Class and Preferred Term (Incidence &gt; 0% in One or More Treatment Groups) (APaT Population)

The percentage of participants with AEs resulting in discontinuation of any drug was higher in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group (42.7%) compared with the cis + gem group (15.7%). When adjusted for exposure the event rate of discontinuation of any drug remained higher in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group. AEs resulting in discontinuation of any study drug in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group for ≥2% of participants were neuropathy peripheral (3.7%), pneumonitis (3.2%), peripheral sensory neuropathy (2.5%), ALT increased and rash (2.0% each). The only AE resulting in discontinuation of any study drug in the cis + gem group was neutropenia (3.3%). The percentage of participants with AEs resulting in discontinuation of any drug was similar in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group (42.7%) compared with the EV + pembrolizumab ISD (49.5%). Drug-related AEs resulting in discontinuation of any drug in ≥2% of participants in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group were peripheral neuropathy (3.7%), pneumonitis (3.2%), peripheral sensory neuropathy (2.5%), and rash (2.0%).

The analysis of discontinuations and interruptions per treatment phases is reported in the specific section above.

## Post marketing experience

Enfortumab vedotin was first approved for marketing in the US on 18-DEC-2019 under accelerated approval, and regular approval was granted on 09-JUL-2021. The safety profile of enfortumab vedotin was summarized in the Periodic Safety Update Report covering the period of 18-DEC-2024 through 17-DEC-2025. The cumulative number of patients receiving enfortumab vedotin since the launch of the product through 17-DEC-2025 is estimated as 153,295.

There are no records of any enfortumab vedotin registration being revoked or withdrawn for safety reasons in any country.

## 2.5.2. Discussion on clinical safety

The safety assessment of perioperative EV+pembrolizumab in the proposed indication is based on data from the pivotal trial EV-304. The EV-304 safety set consists of 403 patients treated with EV+pembrolizumab and 396 treated with neoadjuvant gemcitabine+cisplatin. Additional safety data for the EV+pembrolizumab combination are available for 564 patients from KEYNOTE-869/ EV-103 and KEYNOTE-A39/ EV-302, and safety data for EV monotherapy are available for 793 patients. The median duration of exposure to the combination regimen was 10.2 months in the EV+pembrolizumab arm, which is similar to the EV+pembrolizumab combination safety pool and, as expected, longer than the median duration of exposure in the cisplatin+gemcitabine arm (3.5 months). These safety pools are considered of sufficient size and treatment duration for characterisation of the safety profile of the EV+pembrolizumab combination, although rare adverse drug reactions may not have been detected.

Pooled reference safety data from studies of enfortumab vedotin (EV mono ISD) or pembrolizumab (pembrolizumab RSD) monotherapies are also included to enable a comparison of the safety data of enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab to the established safety profiles of the respective monotherapies. This is considered important for a proper evaluation of the safety profile of each

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

drug in the experimental combination. Moreover, to isolate the contribution of each phase of treatment, data were presented separately for each phase of treatment.

Baseline characteristics were overall well-balanced between treatment arms in KEYNOTE-B15 (see discussion on clinical efficacy).

The collection of safety data was generally acceptable, although the reporting window of nonserious adverse events of 30 days after treatment cessation is on the shorter side for an ADC plus checkpoint inhibitor combination therapy, where 90 days would have been preferable. Importantly, serious adverse events were reported for 90 days after treatment cessation, which is considered appropriate. However, the narrow reporting window for non-serious AEs has likely led to underreporting of some events and is therefore considered to constitute an uncertainty about unfavourable effects.

In KEYNOTE-B15, 98% of patients in both treatment arms experienced at least one adverse event. The incidence of grade ≥3 adverse events was higher in the EV+pembrolizumab arm (75.7%) than in the cisplatin+gemcitabine arm (67.2%), which could be explained by the longer duration of exposure in the EV+pembrolizumab arm. The most common adverse events of any grade in the EV + pembrolizumab arm were pruritus (46.2%), diarrhoea (34.0%), alopecia (31.5%), anaemia (31.3%), decreased appetite (28.5%), nausea (28.3%), fatigue (27.5%), constipation (26.6%), rash (25.1%), and urinary tract infection (25.1%). The most common grade ≥3 adverse events were urinary tract infection (9.9%), neutropenia (7.4%), anaemia (6.5%), hyperglycemia (4.7%), and maculo-papular rash (4.7%). Incidences of all-grade AEs and grade ≥3 AEs were generally similar between the KEYNOTE-B15 EV + pembrolizumab arm and the EV + pembrolizumab ISD. The incidence of serious adverse events 63.3% in the EV + pembrolizumab arm of KEYNOTE-15, which was higher than the observed 48% in the cisplatin + gemcitabine arm, and 47.7% in the EV + pembrolizumab ISD. Not all SAEs were considered drug related (23.6% in the EV+ pembro arm and 10.6% in the cis-gem arm). This is not unexpected considering that this category included serious events typically associated with the surgical intervention of radical cystectomy. In both arms, the most reported SAEs were infectious (UTI, urosepsis, sepsis, pneumonitis) and genitourinary complications (prostate cancer, acute kidney injury).

Adverse events leading to death were more frequent in the EV + pembrolizumab arm (4.2%) than the cisplatin + gemcitabine arm (2.8%), and most events were related to infections/sepsis or unexplained cardiac arrest. The rate of AEs resulting in death was similar across datasets (for datasets see Table 44). However, the comparisons are limited by differences in indication, line of therapy, and treatment (monotherapy), which preclude the identification of specific risk factor for deaths. Absence of a specific correlation between age and risk of death can be noted. In general, the information reported in the SmPC about the risk of infectious complications is considered sufficient to address the risk of complications during the perioperative phase.

Adverse events of special interest to enfortumab vedotin were (numbers in the following are for the EV+pembrolizumab arm of KEYNOTE-B15):

Skin reactions (66% all-grade, 6.2% serious events), including 6 (1.5%) cases of bullous dermatitis, 4 (1.0%) cases of Steven-Johnson syndrome, and 2 (0.5%) cases of acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis. 7.9% of patients discontinued EV due to skin reactions.

Peripheral neuropathy (43.7% all grade, 3% grade ≥3). 6.7% of patients discontinued EV due to peripheral neuropathy. Most events were sensory (41.9%).

Hyperglycaemia (19.6%, 2.2% serious). Three events of type 1 diabetes mellitus and two events of grade 4 diabetic ketoacidosis were observed.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Ocular disorders (30.5%, only one event was grade ≥3). Most events were dry eye (25.1%) and blurred vision 6.2%).

ILD/pneumonitis (7.7%, 3.5% serious, 0 fatal). 6 (1.5%) events led to discontinuation of EV.

Haematological events (anaemia and neutropenia). Incidences were lower in the EV+pembrolizumab arm than in the cisplatin + gemcitabine arm.

Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea (63%, 6% grade ≥3 events, 3% serious events). Most events were diarrhoea (34%).

Skin hyperpigmentation (3.5%).

Rates of AESIs were generally similar between the KEYNOTE-B15 EV+pembrolizumab arm and the EV+pembrolizumab combination therapy ISD.

Analysis per treatment phase allows isolating the contribution of each phase to the general safety evaluation. In particular, the first treatment phase is considered the most critical determinant of whether patients can proceed to the treatment plan.

In the preoperative treatment phase, the nature and frequency of AEs were similar to what was observed throughout the entire observation period of the study and reflects the specific safety profile of both treatments. The reduced frequency of grade 3-5 AEs showed in the pretreatment phase is expected considering the exclusion of the events related to the surgical phase. Slightly more patients in the EV + pembrolizumab arm experienced a delay in undergoing surgery (16.8% vs. 14.4%), but the difference was minimal.

During the surgical phase, the type of AEs reflects the surgical intervention; the number of deaths was higher in the cis-gem arm (9 vs 2) with infectious complications as the main cause of death.

There were slightly more postsurgical adverse events in the EV + pembrolizumab arm (70.7%) than in the cisplatin + gemcitabine arm (65.2%), but similar rates of grade ≥ 3 events (36.2% vs. 35.4%) and serious adverse events (39.0% vs. 39.8%). Fewer patients died from adverse postsurgical events in the EV + pembrolizumab arm (0.6%) than in the cisplatin + gemcitabine arm (2.5%).

## AEOSI for EV

Skin reactions were the most frequently AEOSI identified for EV (66%) followed by Peripheral Neuropathy (43.7%) Ocular Disorders (30.5%), Hyperglicemia (19.6%) and Infusion related reactions (2.5%). The overall incidence of AEOSI foe EV (66%) resulted similar for what reported in the EV+ pembro ISD (70%) and higher in respect to the monotherapy dataset, as expected (57%).

Cutaneous rash was the most frequent skin reaction reported; the cutaneous toxicity of EV is explained considering that the target of enfortumab vedotin, Nectin-4, is expressed in epidermal keratinocytes and skin appendages (eg, sweat glands and hair follicles) and was already reported in the safety profile of EV. The comparison with the ISDs did not show an increased incidence when EV is combined with pembrolizumab (also when incidence was adjusted for exposure), so it could be inferred that risk of skin toxicity does increase non-linearly when both drugs are used in combination.

Peripheral neuropathy, explained by the known effects of MMAE included in EV, was registered in 43.7% of patients in the experimental arm; most of registered cases were defined as sensitive events (41.9%) and mild in grade (2% of grade 3-5). The comparison with other ISDs dataset showed a lower incidence of events (EV+ Pembro ISD 67.4%, EV mono 53.2%); this difference is

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

maintained also in the exposure adjusted dataset. A possible explanation can be identified in the different duration of therapy in respect to the monotherapy setting, in which a longer exposure to EV is permitted and, in respect to EV + Pembro ISD, in the difference in terms of enrolled population, considering that the EV+ Pembro ISD included subjects with a lower ECOG performance status and with a previous chemotherapy before the disease relapse.

The percentage of participants with AEs in the any gastrointestinal nonspecific symptoms group (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) was similar to the one reported in the reference datasets. Gastrointestinal tract is a subjected to EV specific toxicity considering both the nectin-4 expression in various parts of the tract and the specific toxicity due to the MMAE ADCs.

## AEOSI for Pembrolizumab

The incidence of AEOSI for pembrolizumab (47.6%) resulted substantially similar to what reported in the Ev+Pembro ISD (46.8%) and, as expected, higher when compared to the monotherapy of pembrolizumab RSD (27.5%). These findings were similar when incidence was adjusted for exposure. The median time to onset was 46 days (1-449) with a median duration of 77 days (1-1419+). At last follow up, the majority of AEOSI resulted resolved (65.1%) although a 22.9% of subjects were reported with AEOSI not resolved.

In the context of immunotherapy-based treatment, AEOSIs are relevant to the benefit-risk assessment because of their potential effect on treatment continuation, adherence and surgery. The overall number of subjects in which AEOSI were not resolved at the last DCO was 44 (10.9%) in the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab group and 1 (0.3%) in the cis + gem group. The effects of these unresolved AEOSI on the overall treatment plan is deemed negligible, as in the experimental arm treatment discontinuation of any study drug due to them accounted for 1.2% of participants (1.0% discontinuation of pembrolizumab and 0.5% enfortumab vedotin), while dose interruptions of any study drug, pembrolizumab, and enfortumab vedotin occurred in 4 (1.0%) participants, 3 (0.7%) participants, and 4 (1.0%) participants, respectively. The most common not resolved AEOSIs for pembrolizumab were hypothyroidism (6.2%) and severe skin reactions (1.2%), while for EV peripheral neuropathy (17.6%), ocular disorders (6.2%), skin reactions (5.0%) and hyperglycemia (4.5%) were the most commonly reported. Peripheral neuropathy was the only AEOSI that was associated with discontinuation with any study drug (2.7%).

AEOSI had a minor impact on drug discontinuations: 14.9% of drug related AEOSI led to discontinuation at any point of the experimental combined treatment.

Corticosteroid was required in the 54.2% of subjects, with 35.4% of subjects who need high starting dose for AE control.

Laboratory abnormalities were generally consistent with those observed in the EV + pembrolizumab ISD, although more patients had aminotransferase elevations (≥10 x ULN: 4.7% vs. 2.3%, respectively).

The frequency of adverse events leading to discontinuation of any drug was considerably higher in the EV + pembrolizumab arm than the cisplatin + gemcitabine arm of KEYNOTE-B15 (42.7% vs. 15.7%), but similar to that in the EV + pembrolizumab ISD (49.5%).

## Safety in special population

Most of enrolled subjects presented an age &lt; 75 years (88% in both arms), with a minority of subjects between 75-84 years; only 1 subject was &gt; 85 years old and was enrolled in the experimental arm. In general, the incidence of AEs was similar between the three age categories (&lt; 65, 65-74, 75-84, &gt; 85) as well as G 3-5 AEs, while drug-related G 3-5 AE and SAE were higher

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

in the age 75-84 subgroup. This trend can be noted also in the comparator arm and in the pembro mono ISDs dataset, probably reflecting an age-dependant susceptibility in developing AEs. Similarly, the rate of discontinuations was higher in subjects aged &gt; 75 years (50% vs 36.3% in &lt; 65 years). Similar considerations can be applied to ECOG performance status: most of subject enrolled in the trial had ECOG PS 0 (78.6% in the experimental arm and 77% in the control arm). Numerical difference between ECOG PS 0 and 1 makes comparisons difficult: in general, no substantial difference can be noted between subjects with ECOG PS 0 and 1: discontinuations due to drug related AEs were numerically higher in ECOG PS 1 in absence of a clear trend in higher discontinuation rates overall. No clinically relevant differences can be noted in terms of gender, race and region of origin.

## 2.5.3. Conclusions on clinical safety

The safety profile of EV + pembrolizumab in the proposed indication is overall similar to the profile of this combination known from the already approved indication. No new safety concerns were identified.

A justification for not performing a full user consultation with target patient groups on the package leaflet has been submitted by the MAH and has been found acceptable for the following reasons:

The proposed changes do not significantly alter the readability of Padcev PL. Furthermore, since the populations for MIBC and la/mUC are considered to represent the same disease, the results from the previous readability testing remain sufficient to meet the user consultation requirements.

## 3. Benefit-Risk Balance

## 3.1. Therapeutic Context

## 3.1.1. Disease or condition

The final indication is:

Padcev, in combination with pembrolizumab, as neoadjuvant treatment and then continued after radical cystectomy as adjuvant treatment, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with resectable muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC).

## 3.1.2. Available therapies and unmet medical need

Radical cystectomy and pelvic lymph node dissection (RC + PLND) is the mainstay of curative treatment for resectable MIBC {Dong X, et al, UroPrecision. 2023;1:141-61; Matsumoto H, et al, 2019 Int J Urol. 2020) preceded by neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy for patients who can receive it. Adjuvant nivolumab for 1 year showed DFS improvement vs placebo in CHECKMATE274, leading to EU approval in muscle invasive urothelial carcinoma with tumour cell PD-L1 ≥1%, who are at high risk of recurrence after undergoing radical resection (Bajorin DF et al N Engl J Med. 2021 Aug 26;385(9):864). More recently, the results of the Phase 3 NIAGARA study provided a new treatment option for patients with cisplatin-eligible MIBC. The study showed a statistically significant improvement in EFS and OS with perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy (cisplatin + gemcitabine) compared with neoadjuvant cisplatin + gemcitabine followed by RC + PLND (EFS: HR 0.68; 95% CI: 0.56, 0.82; p&lt;0.001; OS: HR 0.75; 95% CI: 0.59, 0.93; p=0.01) (Powles T, et al, N Engl J Med. 2024). Despite the improvement in outcomes demonstrated in the above studies, there remains an unmet need in this setting and the opportunity to further improve clinical outcomes in this patient population.

## 3.1.3. Main clinical studies

The pivotal study is KEYNOTE-B15/ EV-304 study, an ongoing Phase 3, randomized, controlled, parallel-group, multisite, open-label study comparing perioperative enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab with neoadjuvant cisplatin + gemcitabine in participants with cisplatin-eligible muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and with cT2-T4aN0M0 or cT1-T4aN1M0 tumors. A total of 808 adult patients with previously untreated MIBC who were deemed eligible for RC + PLND and planned to undergo standard surgery with curative intent were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive perioperative enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab (Arm A) or neoadjuvant cis + gem (Arm B). Stratification factors were PD-L1 expression (CPS ≥10 vs &lt;10), disease stage (T2N0 vs T3/T4aN0 vs T1-T4aN1), and region (US vs EU vs MOW). The primary endpoint of KN-B15/EV-304 was event free survival (EFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR). Key secondary endpoints were pathological Complete Response (pCR) and overall survival (OS). The results submitted are from the IA1 with DCO of 27-Oct-2025.

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## 3.2. Favourable effects

- The primary endpoint EFS by BICR per RECIST 1.1 demonstrated a statistically significant improvement for the perioperative pembrolizumab + EV treatment compared to standard neoadjuvant cisplatin + gemcitabine. EFS events occurred in 21.5% vs 36.2% of participants, showing HR 0.53 (95%CI 0.41, 0.70) p&lt;0.0001. Kaplan-Meier curves separated from months 6 onwards and remained separated over time, with EFS rates at 12 and 18 months of 86.6% and 82.2% in EV + pembrolizumab arm vs 75.4% and 68.8% in cis-gem arm. Prespecified EFS sensitivity analyses were reported as generally consistent with the primary analysis, including consistency between investigator and BICR-assessed EFS.
- OS results were statistically significant in favour of the perioperative EV + pembrolizumab arm, with HR 0.65 (95%CI 0.48, 0.89; p=0.0029), after 17% vs 24.6% of OS events occurred. After month 6 curves divided with a 5% improvement in OS rate (OS rate at month 12 93.1 vs 89.6%, OS rate at month 18 89.4 vs 84.5%), with medians not reached in either arm.
- pCR was also statistically significant showing improvement for pembrolizumab + EV over standard cis+gem (55.8% vs 32.5%; p&lt;0.0001). The absolute pCR rate for pembrolizumab + EV was similar to the pCR of 57.1% achieved in the cisplatin-ineligible population of KEYNOTE905.

## 3.3. Uncertainties and limitations about favourable effects

The study design does not allow to formally evaluate the contribution of each component (EV and pembrolizumab) of the combination, as well as the contribution of each phase of treatment (neoadjuvant and adjuvant). Nonetheless, the combination of EV and pembrolizumab from the metastatic setting and the clear superiority of the combination shown in KEYNOTE-B15/ EV-304 study attenuates the concern around the individual contribution of each component.

The results supporting this application are based on the first interim analysis of study in KEYNOTEB15/ EV-304 and although more mature data are not considered necessary for this assessment, the final OS results are expected to be submitted post-authorization to further characterize the efficacy in the context of an early curative setting (REC).

## 3.4. Unfavourable effects

Almost all subjects treated with the combination EV+ pembrolizumab experienced at least one adverse event during treatment (98%) and most of them were classified as drug related (96.3%).

63.3% experienced at least one serious adverse events. The most common adverse events of any grade were pruritus (46.2%), diarrhoea (34.0%), alopecia (31.5%), anaemia (31.3%), decreased appetite (28.5%), nausea (28.3%), fatigue (27.5%), constipation (26.6%), rash (25.1%), and urinary tract infection (25.%). The most common grade ≥3 adverse events were urinary tract infection (9.9%), neutropenia (7.4%), anaemia (6.5%), hyperglycaemia (4.7%), and maculopapular rash (4.7%).

4.2% of patients experienced an adverse event leading to death, but most events were related to infections/sepsis or unexplained cardiac arrest.

Adverse events of special interest to enfortumab vedotin are well-known and include skin reactions (of which some can be severe, including 4 cases of Steven-Johnson syndrome), peripheral neuropathy, hyperglycaemia, ocular disorders, ILD/pneumonitis, anaemia, neutropenia, diarrhoea,

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

vomiting, skin hyperpigmentation. Perioperative EV + pembrolizumab did not appear to adversely affect time to surgery or surgical outcomes compared to gemcitabine + cisplatin.

The frequency of adverse events leading to discontinuation of any drug was considerably higher in the EV + pembrolizumab arm than the cisplatin + gemcitabine arm of KEYNOTE-B15 (42.7% vs. 15.7%).

## 3.5. Uncertainties and limitations about unfavourable effects

Non-serious adverse events were only collected for 30 days after treatment cessation, which is considered suboptimal for a checkpoint inhibitor + ADC combination where later adverse drug reactions may be expected. Serious adverse events were collected for 90 days, which is a more appropriate time window which is a more appropriate and reassuring timeframe for analysis of safety.

## 3.7. Benefit-risk assessment and discussion

## 3.7.1. Importance of favourable and unfavourable effects

Overall, KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304 provides evidence of a clinically meaningful benefit of perioperative enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab compared with neoadjuvant cisplatin/gemcitabine in cisplatin-eligible patients with resectable MIBC undergoing radical cystectomy. At the first prespecified interim analysis, the study met its primary endpoint of EFS by BICR and the key secondary endpoint of OS, with statistically significant and clinically meaningful effects. The significantly higher pCR rate further supports the greater activity of neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab. The findings were consistent across predefined subgroups and sensitivity and supplementary analyses, and no adverse effect on the feasibility or completion of surgery was observed. Although the results are based on an interim analysis, the available data are considered sufficient for assessment. Given the early curative setting, the final study results, including final OS data, will be submitted post-authorisation (REC). The study methods were appropriately selected, and changes to the study design and statistical analysis were adequately justified and are not considered to have materially affected the results.

Although a formal comparison would have been ideal in the perioperative setting to assess the contribution of each component to the combination, the supportive evidence for the efficacy of the combination of EV and pembrolizumab from the metastatic setting and the clear superiority of the combination shown in KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304 - study attenuates the concern around the individual contribution of EV. The study design does not allow to disentangle the contribution of each phase

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

(neoadjuvant and adjuvant) to the overall treatment. Therefore, the peri-operative treatment package should be considered in its entirety combination in other and more advanced metastatic settings. No new safety signals were observed.

During the first five months of follow-up, a higher number of deaths due to AEs is reported in the experimental arm: infectious complications remain the main causes of deaths due to AEs in this restricted timeframe. The small number of events during this time frame however does not allow definitive conclusions to be drawn.

## 3.7.2. Balance of benefits and risks

KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304 study showed statistically significant and clinically relevant EFS and OS benefit of perioperative EV + pembrolizumab compared to standard neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy in cisplatin-eligible patients with resectable MIBC undergoing radical cystectomy. The risks related to the toxicity of the combination appear counterbalanced by a clinical benefit in the targeted setting.

## 3.8. Conclusions

The overall B/R is positive.

## 4. Recommendations

## Outcome

Based on the review of the submitted data, the CHMP considers the following variation acceptable and therefore recommends the variation to the terms of the Marketing Authorisation, concerning the following change:

| Variation accepted   | Variation accepted                                                                 | Type              |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| C.6.a                | C.6.a) Addition of a new therapeutic indication or modification of an approved one | Variation type II |

Extension of indication to include Padcev, in combination with pembrolizumab, as neoadjuvant treatment and then continued after radical cystectomy as adjuvant treatment, is indicated for the treatment of adults with resectable muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are eligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy, based on the results from Interim Analysis 1 of the pivotal Study KN-B15 (EV-304); this is a phase 3, randomized, open-label study to evaluate perioperative enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (MK-3475) versus neoadjuvant gemcitabine and cisplatin in cisplatin-eligible participants with Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer. As consequence, sections 4.1, 4.2,4.8, and 5.1 of the SmPC have been updated; the Package Leaflet is updated accordingly. Version 6.3 of the RMP is agreed. In addition, the MAH took the opportunity to bring the PI in line with the latest QRD template version 10.4 and to align with the European Commission guideline on 'Excipients in the labelling and package leaflet of medicinal products for human use' regarding the polysorbate 20 content.

## Amendments to the marketing authorisation

In view of the data submitted with the variation, amendments to Annex(es) I, IIIA, and IIIB and to the Risk Management Plan are recommended.

## Conditions or restrictions with regard to the safe and effective use of the medicinal product

## · Risk management plan (RMP)

The MAH shall perform the required pharmacovigilance activities and interventions detailed in the agreed RMP presented in Module 1.8.2 of the Marketing Authorisation and any agreed subsequent updates of the RMP.

In addition, an updated RMP should be submitted:

At the request of the European Medicines Agency;

Whenever the risk management system is modified, especially as the result of new information being received that may lead to a significant change to the benefit/risk profile or as the result of an important (pharmacovigilance or risk minimisation) milestone being reached.
